We explore the properties of black hole high-mass X-ray binaries (BH-HMXBs) and binary black holes (BBHs) formed under this new framework. We find that a more detailed treatment of MS evolution is necessary to reproduce the high BH masses observed in BH-HMXBs, which are otherwise absent under prescriptions that do not take the internal structure of MS stars into account. Matching the observed rates and orbital periods favors case A mass transfer that is more non-conservative than commonly assumed. We further find that mass transfer of helium-enriched material during case A mass transfer is common in massive binaries, with potential consequences for the structure of the accreting star. For the BBH population, the new MS framework alters the chirp-mass and mass-ratio distributions of detectable mergers, and case A mass transfer can make a substantial contribution to the BBHs formed through the stable mass transfer channel. These systems show a strong preference for near-equal mass ratios, broadly consistent with recent constraints from gravitational-wave observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27197.title: Analytical Chemistry at the Planetary Frontier
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27197.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Planetary science depends on chemical measurements made under conditions very different from those in a terrestrial laboratory. This review treats the analytical methods of planetary science as one connected chain, from orbital remote sensing through in-situ measurements by landers and rovers and sample collection and curation, to the micro-analysis of returned material on Earth. Orbital methods, including visible and near-infrared reflectance, thermal emission and gamma-ray and neutron spectroscopy, are discussed first. In-situ techniques are then reviewed, including laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), micro-focus X-ray fluorescence (XRF), deep-ultraviolet Raman and fluorescence spectroscopy, evolved gas analysis with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and miniaturized mass spectrometry. Contamination control and curation practices are described, followed by laboratory techniques such as secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS and NanoSIMS), atom probe tomography (APT), thermal ionization mass spectrometry (TIMS), synchrotron micro-XRF and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. Accuracy, calibration and reference materials are discussed as the link between in-situ and laboratory data, and the role of chemometrics and data fusion is examined. Flight and laboratory instruments are compared in terms of spatial resolution, detection limit, sample consumption and throughput. Active neutron-gamma spectroscopy planned for the Dragonfly mission to Titan is also discussed. This comparison shows that in-situ and laboratory techniques are complementary. In-situ instruments provide context and select samples, while laboratory techniques provide isotopic, molecular and speciation data that cannot yet be obtained in situ.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27201.title: Ionized Gas Kinematics and Star-forming Clumps in Extremely Metal-poor Galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27201.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27201v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Extremely Metal Poor (XMP) galaxies are the least chemically evolved objects in the local Universe and provide important constraints on galaxy formation in low-metallicity environments. This work investigates the ionised gas kinematics and star formation properties of XMP galaxies to identify disturbed or multi-component gas motions and explore their connection with star formation. We analyse long-slit spectroscopic observations of nine XMP galaxies obtained with the Intermediate Dispersion Spectrograph on the 2.5m Isaac Newton Telescope. The study uses the H$\alpha$ emission line to trace ionised gas and emission-line ratios to derive gas-phase metallicities. The kinematic analysis reveals that some galaxies exhibit ordered rotation, with kinematic centres not always coincident with the luminous star-forming heads. Most systems show disturbed, asymmetric, or declining velocity profiles, while localized distortions near bright star-forming heads suggest that massive clumps influence the surrounding gas dynamics. We derive dynamical masses for the dominant clumps and investigate the mass--metallicity and size--metallicity relations. The clumps exhibit low metallicities consistent with the XMP regime and comparable to those observed in low-mass dwarf galaxies. Three galaxies show counter-rotating or kinematically decoupled ionised-gas components, indicating complex gas kinematics and possible external gas acquisition. Our sample is predominantly composed of isolated systems, with metal-poor star formation concentrated in compact head regions. These properties may reflect gas accretion through mergers, interactions, or the acquisition of metal-poor gas from the intergalactic medium and cosmic filaments. Internal processes such as outflows, gas mixing, recycling, and stochastic star formation may also contribute to the observed properties.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27209.title: Are Dynamical Dark-Energy Cosmologies Old Enough?
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27209.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27209v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent analysis combining baryon acoustic oscillation measurements with cosmic microwave background and Type Ia supernova data show an apparent preference for a time-dependent dark-energy equation of state within $w_0w_a$ parameterizations. Here we test the robustness of this result against an independent cosmological consistency requirement, namely that the expansion history must provide sufficient time to accommodate the oldest observed stellar populations. Motivated by recent stellar and globular-cluster age determinations, we impose progressively stronger lower bounds, $t_0 \geq 13.6$, $13.75$, $13.8$, and $13.85$ Gyr, on the expansion histories allowed by DESI DR2+CMB+Pantheon+ data. We find a systematic displacement of the posterior in the $(w_0,w_a)$ plane toward the $\Lambda$CDM prediction, $(w_0,w_a)=(-1,0)$, as the minimum allowed age is increased. For $t_0 \geq 13.85$ Gyr, the Mahalanobis separation from $\Lambda$CDM decreases from $2.56\sigma$ to $1.72\sigma$, bringing the $\Lambda$CDM prediction inside the 95\% credible region. Our results show that the current evidence for dynamical dark energy is sensitive to independent cosmic-age information and that stellar chronometry provides a direct robustness test of the DESI-favored expansion histories. Requiring sufficiently old cosmologies can appreciably reduce the statistical preference for departures from the standard $\Lambda$CDM model.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27222.title: Large-scale Vortices in the Solar Photosphere: Statistical Properties and the Reliability of Local Correlation Tracking
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27222.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27222v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vortices are observed throughout the solar atmosphere, spanning a wide range of spatial scales. Although small-scale vortices have been studied extensively, mesoscale vortices remain less explored, and it is still unclear whether they can be reliably recovered from observations. Mesogranular-scale motions are recovered from the R2D2 simulations by applying Gaussian spatial smoothing to the horizontal velocity field with full width at half maximum (FWHM) values of 2.5-4.0 Mm. To evaluate the accuracy of local correlation tracking (LCT) and its suitability for identifying mesogranular vortices, we apply LCT to synthetic intensity maps at $\tau = 1$ using the same spatial windows and temporal averaging windows of 10-60 minutes. Vortices are identified in both the reference and LCT-derived velocity fields using the $\Gamma$ method. For all tested parameter combinations, LCT underestimates the number of mesogranular-scale vortices. The best overall recovery is obtained for relatively small spatial smoothing scales (FWHM $\leq 3.5$ Mm) and short averaging windows ($\leq 20$ minutes), which provide the most reliable vorticity and lifetime statistics while maintaining strong agreement in vortex radius and area distributions. Our analysis shows that only a modest fraction of LCT-detected vortices correspond to vortices identified in the reference velocity field (3.54%-17.88%), depending on FWHM and temporal averaging. This indicates that vortex-driven dynamics inferred from LCT-detected vortices should be interpreted with caution. Our results suggest that applying the $\Gamma$ method to LCT-derived velocity fields can recover useful statistical properties of mesoscale vortical structures, especially their temporal trends and characteristic sizes.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27236.title: Searching for Dense Perturbers in Cold Dark Matter Simulations
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27236.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recently, several low-mass, dense perturbers have been inferred from astrophysical observations of gravitational lensing, stellar streams, and satellite galaxies. If interpreted as dark matter subhalos, their inner densities exceed the predictions of the standard cold dark matter (CDM) model. We systematically investigate this tension using a CDM-only zoom-in simulation of a Milky Way analog. We analyze more than 5000 subhalos with masses down to $10^6\,M_\odot$ and reconstruct their inner density profiles using a tidal truncation model. The simulated subhalos are then compared with the observed compact perturbers in terms of their density profiles, enclosed masses, concentrations, and projected cylindrical masses. None of the simulated CDM subhalos is sufficiently dense to reproduce the inferred mass distributions of the observed perturbers. We further examine the redshift evolution of subhalo concentrations and derive a fitting function to characterize this evolution. Our findings motivate further investigations into exceptionally rare formation histories that could produce such dense perturbers, as well as the possibility of physics beyond the standard CDM model.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27251.title: AI and The Enclosure of the Scientific Commons
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27251.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The scientific literature can be viewed as an "information commons:" an intangible resource that "no one owns and is shared by everyone." There are well-established economic and political frameworks for understanding such commons, emerging from the history of agricultural common lands found in places like preindustrial England. This article provides a primer on the history and these frameworks, and considers a key difference between the information commons and the fields of yore: while information commons are robust and immensely valuable --- some can be said to rank among humanity's greatest achievements --- the English agricultural commons no longer meaningfully exist. The latter are gone not because of the well-known "tragedy of the commons," but rather a phenomenon known as the enclosure movement (~1600--1800) that transformed the common lands into private property. Many observers, then and now, judge enclosure to have been theft at a societal scale. This article argues that artificial intelligence (AI) provides precisely the tools needed to enable a previously-infeasible enclosure of the information commons. Although AI-enabled enclosure does not operate identically to physical enclosure, it shares the key features of turning the commons into private wealth and undermining the social systems that support them (via "slop spam"). The concepts presented in this article can provide a scholarly basis for interrogating the foreboding feeling that AI may represent not just a smash-and-grab, but an attack upon a whole way of life.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27252.title: J-PLUS: Identifying Outlier Spectral Energy Distributions in the Fourth Data Release Using Unsupervised Machine Learning
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27252.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27252v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The selection of candidates belonging to rare or underrepresented stellar populations, as well as novel objects, is essential for spectroscopic follow-up. In this work, we demonstrate how combining broad- and narrow-band photometric information with machine-learning techniques enables this selection. Using photometric data in twelve filters from the Javalambre Photometric Local Universe Survey (J-PLUS) as input, we applied an anomaly detection technique based on autoencoders to identify spectral energy distributions (SEDs) that deviate from the dominant pattern in the J-PLUS objects sample. Subsequently, we applied the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) algorithm to the J-PLUS colors of the outlier SEDs population. Combining information from the SIMBAD database and other astronomical surveys to classify the outliers identified by the autoencoder, we are able to characterize over-densities in the t-SNE map. Our study specifically focuses on well-defined islands in the t-SNE space, corresponding to specific populations. We identified a large sample of white dwarfs and low-mass stars, including a small subset of polluted white dwarfs, and report potential candidates for spectroscopic follow-up, including 19 carbon-rich stars, 11 cataclysmic variables and 170 white-dwarfs-main-sequence binaries, all previously unreported in the literature.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27282.title: The Future of Gamma-Ray Bursts as Probes of the Epoch of Reionization in the Era of JWST and the Extremely Large Telescope
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27282.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27282v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Epoch of Reionization (EoR) is a key era of cosmological history that remains poorly understood. An examination of the Ly-alpha damping wing of high-redshift GRBs can provide direct measurements of the fraction of neutral hydrogen (i.e., neutral fraction) of the IGM in the vicinity of the GRB host galaxy, in addition to the neutral column in the host along the sight-line to the GRB. The latter quantity can help infer the fraction of ionizing photons escaping the galaxy (i.e. escape fraction); the average escape fraction being a key input to EoR models. New and upcoming observatories such as the JWST and the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) can obtain more robust estimates of the hydrogen column density and neutral fraction around high-redshift GRBs. We simulate spectra for the JWST NIRSpec and ELT HARMONI spectrographs using different GRB magnitudes and exposure times to determine their capabilities for measuring column densities and neutral fractions with the Ly-alpha damping wings of high-redshift GRBs. We find that both spectrographs will be highly effective for obtaining column density estimates. Despite the presence of telluric lines, we find that ELT HARMONI will be a powerful instrument for retrieving accurate neutral fraction estimates, but JWST NIRSpec will be vital for obtaining neutral fraction measurements for bright GRBs that fall in redshift ranges where ELT is less effective. Additionally, shorter JWST Target of Opportunity (ToO) follow-up times would greatly increase the accuracy of neutral fraction estimates obtained with NIRSpec spectra.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27287.title: The presence and order of QCD phase transitions from gravitational-wave observations of neutron star mergers
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27287.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27287v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of neutron star mergers allows us to probe the dense portion of the nuclear equation of state. We develop a formalism for testing the existence and order of phase transitions in the cores of neutron stars using only gravitational-wave observations of their inspiral. We test our formalism on data from the first binary neutron star mergers GW170817 and GW190425, and use synthetic injections assuming the next and uber-next upgrades of the LIGO observatories, A+ and A#, as well as with Cosmic Explorer. We show that populations of mergers in either A+ or A# will be able to measure the existence of a first-order phase transition in observations lasting less than one PhD (less than half a US PhD!). On the other hand, with only the inspiral, we cannot distinguish populations of neutron stars with no phase transition from those with second- or third-order phase transitions or with first-order phase transitions with relatively large transition densities.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27303.title: Globular Clusters GMRT Pulsar Survey (GCGPS) III: ORION - a multi-beam acceleration search pipeline
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27303.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27303v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Globular clusters host rich millisecond pulsar populations, but the known population remains incomplete. We present the observing strategy for Phase II of the Globular Clusters GMRT Pulsar Survey (GCGPS), which uses the SPOTLIGHT system to form 160 synthesised beams simultaneously, substantially expanding the instantaneous field of view compared with the two phased-array beams of Phase I. The configuration is tunable through the beam overlap and the number of contributing antennas, allowing spatial coverage to be balanced against sensitivity. We quantify the sensitivity losses from intra-channel dispersion smearing and finite sampling, which motivate the adopted dispersion-measure limits of 50 and 150 pc/cc for Bands 3 and 4. To process the resulting data, we introduce ORION, a GPU-accelerated pipeline that combines the high-throughput Fourier-domain filtering of PULSCAN with localised parameter refinement using PRESTO. In single-beam tests with simulated binary pulsars, ORION reduces processing time by a factor of approximately 15 to 30 relative to the CPU-based Phase I pipeline, with comparable or higher folded detection significance. On-sky validation with Cycle 49 observations recovered four known globular cluster pulsars with spin periods of approximately 5.4 to 406 ms. Using eight GPUs and 64 CPU cores, ORION processes full 160-beam observations in approximately 0.25 to 0.33 times the observation duration, corresponding to three to four times real-time throughput. Together, the Phase II strategy and ORION provide a scalable framework for expanding globular cluster pulsar searches, with future development targeting highly accelerated and jerked binary systems.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27311.title: Source velocities of fast radio bursts constrained by their dispersion measure variations
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27311.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27311v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Growing evidence suggests that many fast radio bursts (FRBs) originate from extragalactic magnetars. Like all neutron stars, magnetars may be kicked at birth to large velocities, the values of which directly inform the physics governing stellar explosions and compact object formation. A subset of repeating FRBs show significant variability in their dispersion measures (i.e., electron column densities) over time, often exhibiting apparently secular trends. Here we show that all repeating FRBs with significant dispersion measure variations can be generically explained by motion of the source. We use existing measurements to constrain the minimum space velocities of the FRB sources, which are found to be $\gtrsim 20-2800\,{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$. We simultaneously constrain the plasma properties of the circumsource media, which are comparable to those of compact HII regions. For sources with compact radio nebulae, we directly infer the maximum source ages, and find them to be consistent with the ages of known Galactic magnetars. Our findings suggest that significant DM variability is a hallmark of young sources born with natal kicks through prompt formation channels. Applying our methods to a larger sample with continued monitoring of repeating FRB dispersion measures will reveal key physics of compact object formation.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27312.title: SN 2023iop: An Extreme 1987A-like Supernova and the Death of Very Massive Stars
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27312.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27312v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Supernova (SN) 1987A showed that some hydrogen-rich core-collapse supernovae (SNe) rise slowly to peak, defining a distinct subclass. Wide-field surveys have uncovered more extreme members, such as OGLE-2014-SN-73, SN 2020faa, and SN 2023vbw, that challenge neutrino-driven explosion models. We present ultraviolet-to-infrared, radio, X-ray, and spectropolarimetric observations of SN 2023iop at $z = 0.1020$, the most extreme 87A-like event to date. It rose for $\gtrsim88$ rest-frame days to $M_r \approx -20.1$ mag, also placing it among the hydrogen-rich superluminous SNe, and radiated $\gtrsim4\times10^{50}$ erg. Its spectra resemble those of typical Type II SNe and remain photospheric at $\sim330$ days post-maximum. Continuum polarization of 0.8-1.0% indicates an aspherical system. Hydrogen-rich pair-instability supernova (PISN) models of a $190~M_\odot$ star reproduce the light-curve up to 150 days after peak, but not the late-time emission. A late-time spectrum shows a feature near 7300 {\AA}, tentatively identified as [Ni II] $\lambda$7378. The implied $\approx0.02~M_\odot$ of stable $^{58}$Ni is reached only in the most massive PISN models. The low-mass host galaxy ($\sim10^{8.2}~M_\odot$) is consistent with a metal-poor progenitor as required by the PISN channel. Fallback accretion reproduces the light-curve morphology, but not the colors. We consider a pair-instability explosion the most plausible scenario, with the late-time light-curve excess powered by circumstellar interaction, which shows no signatures in the spectra. SN 2023iop shows that the most luminous 87A-like events occupy an underexplored region of massive-star evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27328.title: Core-Collapse Supernova Rates in the Dark Energy Survey
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27328.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27328v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Over its five-year campaign (2013-2017), the Dark Energy Survey (DES) supernova (SN) survey recorded 31,636 light curves. Using a custom-built, two-stage random forest classifier, we identified 2,445 likely core-collapse SNe (CC SNe) within the survey rate analysis footprint. With this sample, we measure the volumetric CC SN rate from redshift z = 0 to 1.3 in 11 redshift bins, representing the most detailed single-survey coverage to date across nine billion years of lookback time. Over this interval, the CC SN rates are well fit by a power law R_CC(z) = R_0 (1 + z)^\alpha, with R_0 = 1.58 \pm 0.17 \times 10^{-4} \text{ yr}^{-1} \text{ Mpc}^{-3} and \alpha = 2.85 \pm 0.25. The rate turnover, expected at cosmic noon, is not yet apparent. Because CC SNe trace recent star formation, we compare our measurements with recent cosmic star-formation history (CSFH) models. Our measurements are ~70 per cent higher than CSFH models using a Salpeter initial mass function (IMF) to predict CC SN rates. Replacing the Salpeter IMF with a Baldry and Glazebrook IMF and a CC SN progenitor mass range of 8-40 M_\odot bridges the gap. Alternatively, CSFHs may miss a hitherto unidentified population of low-luminosity galaxies. We further find that the local ratio of stripped-envelope (SE) SNe to all CC SNe is 31 \pm 5 per cent, remaining constant from z = 0 to 1.3. Combined with an IMF analysis accounting for the "missing progenitor problem" of hydrogen-rich SNe, our results favour a mixture of single massive stars and binaries as SE SN progenitors, with the redshift-invariant ratio favouring binary channels.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27453.title: Size, Albedo, and Taxonomy of Asteroid (1201) Strenua from Stellar Occultation and ATLAS Photometry
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27453.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27453v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context. A multi-chord stellar occultation by (1201) Strenua observed on 26 April 2026 is combined with ATLAS $c$- and $o$-band photometry.
  Aims. We aim to determine the size and geometric albedo of Strenua and reassess its taxonomic classification.
  Methods. Four positive chords from a 47-station campaign across Indonesia were fitted within a Bayesian forward-modeling framework to derive an ellipse cross-section and equivalent diameter. ATLAS photometry was modeled using the $H, G_1, G_2$ phase-function system to determine band-specific absolute magnitudes, converted to $H_{\mathrm{V}}$, and combined with the occultation diameter to calculate geometric albedo and update taxonomy.
  Results. The chords yield semi-axes $a' = 27.49^{+3.90}_{-1.65}$~km and $b' = 14.33^{+2.37}_{-2.69}$~km (position angle $95.3^{+4.9}_{-2.7}$ deg), giving an area-equivalent diameter $D_{\mathrm{eq}} = 39.86^{+2.06}_{-1.66}$~km. Photometric modeling gives $H_c = 11.50 \pm 0.05$~mag ($G_{1,c} = 0.81 \pm 0.08$, $G_{2,c} = 0.04 \pm 0.02$) and $H_o = 11.29^{+0.02}_{-0.03}$~mag ($G_{1,o} = 0.94^{+0.03}_{-0.05}$, $G_{2,o} = 0.01 \pm 0.01$), yielding $H_{\mathrm{V}} = 11.46 \pm 0.05$~mag. The resulting geometric albedo $p_{\mathrm{V}} = 0.029 \pm 0.003$ places Strenua among the darkest primitive asteroids, securely reclassifying it as P-class and resolving its legacy X-complex ambiguity.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27484.title: Exomoonlight Sonata: On the Fate of Exomoons Around Migrating White Dwarf Planets
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27484.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27484v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The survival of exomoons around close-in white dwarf planets offers a potential constraint on their migration histories and an alternative pathway to post-main-sequence habitability. We investigate whether moons can survive the tidal circularization of planets via high-eccentricity migration, and consider a hierarchical three-body system (white dwarf-planet-moon) after an initial eccentricity excitation of the planetary orbit. Using an analytic equilibrium tidal model, we compare the evolution of the planetary and satellite orbits and examine the conditions required for an evection resonance. We show that the moons of pseudosynchronously rotating planets always migrate inwards since the planetary corotation radius always exceeds the Hill radius, independent of mass and orbital eccentricities. Comparing the migration timescales for the moon and the planet shows that compact moons undergo rapid tidal decay relative to the outer orbit. However, the wider separations favored by slower migration timescales experience pericenter perturbations whose work constitutes a substantial fraction of the moon's orbital energy. Together, our results indicate that moons likely do not survive during a planet's high-eccentricity migration phase in a three-body configuration.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27489.title: Constraining the FRB Central Engine from Flux Variations of Persistent Radio Sources: FRB 20240114A as the First Attempt
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27489.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27489v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Some repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) are associated with persistent radio sources (PRSs), likely driven by the long-term activity of a central engine. We investigate FRB 20240114A-currently the most active repeating FRB-to explore the link between its burst activity and the flux variability of its associated PRS. We model electrons responsible for FRB emission being continuously injected from a central magnetar into its magnetar wind nebula (MWN), where synchrotron radiation produces the PRS. Comparing our model with the latest PRS spectra and flux variations, we constrain the physical properties of the FRB source. We find that the total energy injected into the MWN during FAST observations from January to August 2024 is $\sim 10^{48} \, \rm{erg}$, consistent with the magnetic energy budget of a magnetar with an internal magnetic field of $\sim 10^{16} \, \rm G$. The bulk Lorentz factor of the FRB-emitting plasma is mildly constrained to $\lesssim 10^3$, and FRB 20240114A is inferred to be powered by a young magnetar aged $\sim 10$-$20 \, \rm {yr}$. These results show that the PRS flux variability effectively probes FRB emission properties. We predict that while PRS luminosity increases rapidly with enhanced FRB activity, it will slowly fade over decades via adiabatic cooling after FRB activity ceases. Energetics suggest that the hyper-active phase observed in FRB 20240114A (burst rate $\sim 700 \, \rm hr^{-1}$) is a rare state with a duty cycle of $\lesssim 10^{-2}$, which is broadly consistent with its detection rate in current FRB-PRS samples.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27526.title: A $\wedge$-like metallicity profile in the disk of the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27526.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27526v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unveiling the properties of the progenitors that formed the tidal structures of the Milky Way (MW) is essential for exploring the MW's assembly history. Such studies further afford a unique opportunity to dissect the formation and evolution of dwarf galaxies by contrasting surviving and disrupted systems. However, reconstructing the intrinsic structure of progenitors solely from the positions and velocities of their tidal debris remains a formidable challenge. Here, we decode the chemo-kinematic signatures embedded in the stellar streams of the Sagittarius (Sgr) dwarf galaxy through N-body simulations. Our simulation reproduces a vertical metallicity gradient in the Sgr streams. We show that this feature is naturally explained if the stream originated from a disk component with a $\wedge$-like metallicity profile. Remarkably, similar metallicity profiles are identified in MaNGA survey data for a few (3/217) field dwarf galaxies, suggesting this feature is rare but not unique to Sgr. The vertical metallicity gradient of stellar streams preserves extra detailed galactic fossil records, enabling quantitative reconstruction of the peculiar structure of the satellite galaxy. The similar metallicity profiles of Sgr and MW raise the question of a possible special coevolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27621.title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27621.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27621v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly being deployed into radiation-challenging environments in spacecraft, particle accelerators, and, soon, space-based data centers. Instantiated as a learned orchestration of numbers stored in persistent memory, models are susceptible to continual degradation as high-energy particles corrupt data. At inference time, new data passed through the network fundamentally break the off-line assumptions and guarantees of a static model determined during training. To preserve the quality and efficacy of the models, fault tolerance against bit flips is a clear objective. In this work we developed a runtime method for repairing the quantized weights of neural networks (NNs) after bit flips on commodity, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware, without storing extra replicas. Our work extends the well-established Fault-Aware Training (FAT) paradigm by adding an alignment penalty to concentrate undamaged activations and weights into a low-rank subspace, and we then reconstruct flagged corrupted coordinates from the uncorrupted survivors. We call this method {\it Projection Healing} and apply it to six regression benchmarks on quantized NNs. Holding a FAT checkpoint fixed and toggling only the runtime heal gives a further ${\sim}23\%$ reduction in the native-unit excess integral. Across those datasets the method extends the operational scrub interval by a median of $2.04\times$ at a $+5\%$ RMSE degradation and $1.96\times$ at $+50\%$, compared with $1.62\times$ and $1.07\times$ for classical Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection (SECDED). This introduces a new path towards designing resilient data-driven models, complementing established hardware redundancy, ECC, and FAT-based techniques.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27635.title: Probing Nearby Electron Sources and Local Diffusion with the TeV All-Electron Spectrum
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27635.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Radiative losses restrict multi-TeV cosmic-ray electrons to young nearby accelerators, allowing the all-electron spectrum (electrons plus positrons) to retain information about particle release and local transport. We investigate how a nearby source can shape this spectrum using Vela as a representative example. We compare a birth-time burst with continuous release for the same total injected electron energy and examine the dependence on the diffusion coefficient, injection index, and source energetics. The burst spectrum develops a cooling-limited boundary near 28 TeV at the age of Vela, whereas continuous release produces a broader high-energy tail through the contribution of recently injected particles. The flux at Earth is largest over a finite range of diffusion coefficients, reflecting the competition between inefficient arrival and spatial dilution. Harder injection spectra and larger released energies increase the source contribution in the multi-TeV region, and we map the combinations of injection index and released electron energy that can produce an observable spectral feature. For anisotropic diffusion, the source visibility also depends on the angle between the Vela-Earth direction and the local ordered magnetic field. Future direct measurements extending the all-electron spectrum beyond several TeV could therefore distinguish different release histories and constrain both the energetics of nearby sources and local cosmic-ray transport.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27708.title: Short-timescale X-ray variability of the blazar 1ES 1959+650 observed with AstroSat/SXT
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27708.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27708v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyse the AstroSat Soft X-ray Telescope (SXT) observation of the high-synchrotron-peaked blazar 1ES 1959+650 taken on 2023 September 2, which covers 362 ks with about 95 ks of good exposure. We build 0.6-7 keV light curves in six sub-bands, binned at 5830 s (the orbital period) and 1000 s. All sub-bands show excess variance, with fractional variability of 3.7 to 6.5 per cent that increases with energy ($\propto E^{0.32\pm0.07}$). The power spectrum of the total band, fitted with a model that includes the window function of the orbital gaps, is a red-noise power law with slope $-1.80$ (95 per cent range $-2.8$ to $-1.4$). A Lomb-Scargle search finds no significant periodicity (global $p>0.57$) and would have detected, with 90 per cent probability, a sinusoid with an rms amplitude above 1.9 to 3.7 per cent at periods of 3 to 50 ks. The soft (0.6-1.4 keV) and hard (1.9-7 keV) light curves are correlated near zero lag, but only marginally (global $p=0.04$ and 0.07 for power-spectrum slopes of $-1.7$ and $-2.0$), and the lag is $-1^{+6}_{-10}$ ks, consistent with zero. No pair of sub-bands that includes 0.6-0.8 keV shows a significant correlation or lag, so an energy-dependent lag of a few ks can be neither confirmed nor excluded. The 0.6-7 keV light curve contains one hump with rise and decay times of about 0.4 to 0.6 d, which is only marginally distinguishable from red noise ($p\approx0.05$ to $0.07$). The count rate distribution is consistent with a lognormal distribution, and the hardness ratio does not depend significantly on flux.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27733.title: Gaussian process-based Bayesian imaging of bolometric (sub-)millimetre data
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27733.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Widefield single-dish telescopes operating at (sub-)mm wavelengths ($\lambda \sim 4$~mm to 350~$\mu$m) tend to feature much faster mapping speeds than radio interferometers at the same wavelengths, and are more suitable for measuring signals on larger spatial scales. However, the data are dominated by atmospheric fluctuations on large scales and by photon and instrumental noise on smaller scales, making it difficult to recover the true astronomical sky. We build on maria-nifty, a Gaussian process-based Bayesian imaging framework for reconstructing sky maps from single-dish telescope data, implemented on top of Numerical Information Field Theory (NIFTy). It uses modular generative models to efficiently separate the astronomical signal from atmospheric emission while providing pixel-wise uncertainty quantification for the reconstructed sky maps. Moreover, our method cleanly separates individual astrophysical signals, even though they are superposed on the sky. Following its successful validation on synthetic time-ordered data generated using the maria software, we apply it to real data observed with the MUSTANG-2 bolometric array on the 100-meter Green Bank Telescope. For the galaxy cluster RXJ1347.5-1145, we separate the extended cluster emission from the compact source at its centre and obtain a smoother map with fewer artefacts compared to a standard maximum-likelihood reconstruction using the same data. The JAX-based implementation and GPU acceleration provide the basis for applying the method to the vastly larger datasets that the next generation of single-dish telescopes will deliver.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27742.title: Estimator Precision and Selection for Up-the-Ramp Sampling with a High-Read-Noise InGaAs Camera
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27742.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27742v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The noise properties of an InGaAs camera vary with gain, requiring a trade-off between implementation complexity and precision. Using generalized least squares (GLS) with known covariance as the precision benchmark, we examine the applicability and precision penalties of ordinary least squares (OLS) and correlated double sampling (CDS) at different noise operating points. We define $\eta=fT/\sigma_\mathrm{R}^2$, where $f$ is the total pixel count rate, $T$ the fitting span, and $\sigma_\mathrm{R}$ the single-read noise. For constant flux, uniform sampling, and independent white read noise plus Poisson noise, established finite-sampling variance expressions give equal OLS and CDS variances at $\eta=10$ for $N\ge4$ reads; OLS is favored below this boundary and CDS above it. Analytical and Monte Carlo comparisons for three gain modes quantify the precision loss of the better simplified estimator relative to GLS. In high-gain on-sky data, choosing OLS at 20 s and CDS at 90 s increases the background residual standard deviation by 3.55% and 3.01%, respectively, relative to two-iteration feasible GLS (FGLS). Photometry of 21 common sources does not clearly resolve most estimator differences. The observed OLS-CDS crossover occurs earlier than the ideal prediction, indicating that temporal covariance beyond the ideal model also affects the selection boundary. Observational validation is limited to high gain; medium- and low-gain choices rely on theory and simulations using calibrated parameters. OLS or CDS can replace GLS with a small precision penalty at suitable operating points. The ideal criterion provides an initial selection rule, whose practical boundary requires validation against observed temporal covariance.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27775.title: An improved self-gravity treatment in general relativistic smoothed particle hydrodynamics
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27775.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27775v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General relativistic smoothed particle hydrodynamics (GRSPH) on a fixed black hole (BH) spacetime is suitable for fluid bodies that are much less massive than the BH, but the self-gravity of the fluid is added as an extra term in the equation of motion. Standard GRSPH implementations add this as a Newtonian source term to the momentum equation, which is no longer valid when the fluid moves at a sizeable fraction of the speed of light, close to the BH. We develop an improved prescription by deriving the weak gravitational field of each fluid element in its local rest frame and transforming it to the global frame where the momentum equation is solved. The resulting force uses rest-frame distances and softening lengths, accounts for the time dilation of the receiving particle, and its motion relative to the source particle. The derivation applies to any weakly self-gravitating flow on a fixed BH background, provided the body is small compared with its distance from the BH. Implemented in a tree-based GRSPH code, the prescription reproduces the self-gravity of a boosted polytrope with a median error below 1\% up to a Lorentz factor of 2, and keeps a binary of two polytropes stable over ten orbits. As an application, we study tidal disruption events (TDEs) of solar-type stars by supermassive BHs. The treatment of self-gravity shifts the disruption threshold and changes both the remnant core mass and the debris energy distribution. Newtonian self-gravity leaves substantial surviving cores in encounters that our prescription predicts to be nearly complete disruptions.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27778.title: Cosmic-ray melt windows in interstellar ice make a four-carbon ketose but not the sugar pattern of G+0.693-0.027
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27778.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27778v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Erythrulose (ERU), a four-carbon (C4) ketose, is reported towards the Galactic-centre cloud G+0.693-0.027 at a column density comparable to that of glycolaldehyde (GA), while the three-carbon (C3) sugars are not detected. We test whether melt windows opened in interstellar ice by cosmic-ray heavy ions can reproduce this pattern, with each rate fixed to a published value where available. A track model for eleven cosmic-ray nuclei determines the rate and duration of the liquid windows and the energy deposited inside and outside the melts. A radical network including C1 radicals from formaldehyde and methanol follows the inventory through repeated events. Radiolysis between events uses measured half-life doses of organics in cold ice. Hydrated GA opens a channel that preferentially forms the C4 ketose, so the melt-window chemistry can account for the ketose identity of ERU, although cold surface chemistry also yields it. The overall pattern, however, is not reproduced. The C1 radicals add one carbon at a time: dihydroxyacetone is at 15 times its limit when ERU/GA reaches the observed value. The ions deposit 0.41 eV per molecule per event outside the melts, which destroys the sugars between events; the ratio is reached only for half-life doses above 1000 eV, against measured values below 5 eV. The exposure is less certain: 2940 whole-grain melting events, 65 Myr at an ionisation rate $\zeta=10^{-14}$ s$^{-1}$. Within 7 Myr it needs $\zeta\gtrsim9.3\times10^{-14}$ s$^{-1}$, 9.3 times the dense-gas limit in the Central Molecular Zone, or $5.8\times10^{-15}$ s$^{-1}$ if the trapped radicals recombine. With standard assumptions the sugars of G+0.693 are not made in cosmic-ray melt windows. The pattern would need C1 radicals that do not add to the sugar radicals, sugars that survive the solid-phase dose and a local source of MeV ions with $\zeta\gtrsim2\times10^{-13}$ s$^{-1}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27788.title: When the core ate the atmosphere
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27788.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27788v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The initial volatile element inventories in a planet's atmosphere, mantle, and core are established by delivery and transport during planetary growth. Conversely, the volatile abundances of Earth's planetary reservoirs record its accretion pathway. We model here volatile transport during planet formation for two different delivery scenarios, via pebble and planetesimal accretion, to predict the volatile inventories of proto-Earth at the end of its main accretion phase. We find that the distributions of volatiles between the atmosphere, mantle, and core exhibit strong sensitivity to volatile delivery timing, metal-silicate partition coefficients, atmosphere-magma solubilities, and planet mass. In particular, the early volatile delivery expected in pebble accretion scenarios substantially enhances core sequestration of hydrogen and carbon relative to continuous delivery during incremental planetesimal accretion. With our fiducial partition coefficients, the pebble accretion model produces a 760 bar carbon-dominated atmosphere with 39 bar of hydrogen and water and a few bars of nitrogen, consistent with volatile concentration estimates for bulk silicate Earth including the atmosphere. The corresponding planetesimal accretion model produces a more massive ($\sim$$1350$ bar) atmosphere with similar composition. The core stores $\sim$$70$% of both the H and the C budget in the early-delivery scenario, but $\lesssim$$50$% in the corresponding continuous delivery scenario. Overall our results demonstrate that substantial amounts of volatiles are sequestered into rocky planet cores during planet formation and that the volatile inventory of bulk silicate Earth was likely established already during the magma ocean phase of planet formation.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27806.title: Probing the Optical/UV Continuum Variability of Active Galactic Nuclei with the Damped Random Walk Model
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27806.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27806v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Optical/UV continuum variability over baselines of up to 20 yr is investigated using the damped random walk (DRW) model for 1214 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) compiled from Y. Shen et al. and C. J. Burke et al. Among these, 115 AGNs with reliable DRW fitting and unbiased DRW parameters (timescale $\tau_{2500}$ and amplitude $\sigma_{2500}$ at the rest-frame 2500~\AA) are used to examine the relations between the variability and the accretion properties. We found a significant correlation of $\tau_{2500}$ with black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) and dimensionless accretion rate ($\dot{\mathscr{M}}$) of the form $\tau_{2500} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{0.50\pm0.07} \dot{\mathscr{M}}^{0.27\pm0.04}$, while the dependence on the continuum luminosity at 5100~\AA\ and redshift becomes insignificant after controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$. $\tau_{2500}$ also correlate with the mass accretion rate ($\dot{M}$) as $\tau_{2500} \propto \dot{M}^{0.41\pm0.04}$, which is consistent with the thermal timescale expected from the standard thin-disk model within $3\sigma$ uncertainties; while the average value is consistent with the expectations of the model, the scatter in the relation can be due to differences in the viscosity parameter ($\alpha$) or in disk temperature profiles. Assuming that \tauuv\ corresponds to the accretion disk thermal timescale, the disk-emitting radius at rest-frame 2500~\AA\ ($R_{2500}$) is found to correlate with $M_{\rm BH}$ as $R_{2500} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{0.53\pm0.05}$. Using the microlensing-based $R_{2500}-M_{\rm BH}$ relation of C. W. Morgan et al., $\alpha$ is statistically estimated to be $0.04\pm0.01$.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27807.title: What Shapes the Ultraviolet Spectra of Type Ia Supernovae?
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27807.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27807v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) observations of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit significant diversity, but their physical origin remains poorly understood. We investigate UV spectra of SNe Ia observed with the Swift UltraViolet and Optical Telescope. Our expanded pre-maximum sample probes dependencies on decline rate, ejecta properties, and host environment. We recover the correlation between UV flux and decline rate near maximum in the near-UV (NUV), and find correlations at pre-maximum phases in both the NUV and mid-UV (MUV). This trend is strongly wavelength dependent, with slow decliners showing higher NUV but lower MUV flux than fast decliners. Synthetic TARDIS spectra varying the 56Ni abundance show that enhanced 56Ni suppresses the MUV while increasing the NUV, broadly reproducing the trend. We find no significant correlation between UV flux and ejecta velocity, while Si II 6355 pEW shows trends similar to those with decline rate. We also find no significant correlations with host-galaxy properties, although host environment may contribute to the remaining UV diversity among SNe with similar decline rates. Early-excess SNe show enhanced flux mainly in the NUV rather than a broad UV excess, suggesting that strong circumstellar interaction is not necessarily required to explain the observed excess emission. Peculiar subclasses show distinct UV properties, with brighter and hotter subclasses showing higher UV flux, although the current sample is small and does not cover all SN Ia subtypes. Our results suggest that the UV diversity of SNe Ia is shaped by multiple mechanisms that contribute differently across the UV wavelength range.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27831.title: The chemical evolution of the LMC from APOGEE abundances: a hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27831.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27831v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star-formation histories that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution. We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $[\mathrm{Mg}/\mathrm{Fe}]$-$[\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}]$ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star-formation efficiency (SFE). We selected 4933 LMC red-giant-branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code OMEGA+. The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, star-formation history (SFH), present-day mass partition, SFR, and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with an RMS residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at $t_2=10.39$ Gyr and with integrated mass ratio $M_2/M_1=0.159$, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centred at $t=11.91$ Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range. A hybrid second-infall and SFE-enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN-rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27876.title: Single-Parameter Exponential Model Outperforms Standard Dark Matter and Modified Newtonian Frameworks in Predicting Galactic Rotation Curves
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27876.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27876v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The functional forms of galactic rotation curves provide a fundamental test for models of gravity and dark matter. In this work, we conduct a rigorous statistical comparison of five distinct models against the complete sample of 175 galaxies from the SPARC database. The models under consideration are: (1) a one-parameter empirical law, physically constrained by each galaxy's measured flat disc rotation velocity ($V_{\text{flat}}$); (2) a classical two-parameter Freeman disk; (3) a three-parameter Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) dark matter halo plus baryons model; (4) a one-parameter Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) model; and (5) a two-parameter Bosma/Dark Matter Disk model. We employ a Bayesian framework with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for parameter estimation, and use the Akaike Information Criterion (AICc) to assess the goodness-of-fit and statistical parsimony of the best-fit models. Our results reveal a decisive preference for the constrained one-parameter empirical model. It is selected as the best descriptor for a clear majority of the sample (60.6\%) and, critically, also achieves the best median goodness-of-fit, with a reduced chi-squared of $\chi^2_{\nu} = 0.41$. In contrast, the standard NFW framework is preferred in only 12.6\% of cases, while the MOND and Freeman disk models are selected as optimal for just 10.3\% and 9.1\%, respectively. The Bosma model, despite linking dynamics to the gas distribution, is preferred in only 7.4\% of cases. The pronounced statistical and descriptive success of this simple, physically-anchored law over more complex, established theories suggests that its functional form represents a fundamental and highly efficient organizing principle in the dynamics of disk galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27925.title: A bright X-ray flaring event from the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient IGR J00370+6122 observed with NuSTAR
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27925.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an analysis of a long NuSTAR observation of the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient (SFXT) IGR J00370+6122, obtained around the peak of its orbital modulation. The observation has a net exposure ~93 ks. During the observation, the source displayed a bright flaring event that was resolved into numerous short flares with durations of 10-1000 s. The 3-70 keV luminosity spanned a dynamic range of ~200, from ~1E34 to ~1.8E36 erg/s; the maximum was reached for only ~40 s in total. The spectrum is well described by an absorbed double-Comptonisation model, with parameters consistent with those found in other X-ray pulsars accreting at similarly low luminosities. This is the first detection of a double-hump continuum in IGR J00370+6122, which extends this spectral state to the class of intermediate SFXTs. We searched for the previously reported ~346 s and ~674 s periodicities and find no significant signal at either period, which makes their interpretation as the neutron star spin period less likely. Using ~21 yr of Swift/BAT monitoring, we refine the orbital period of the system to P_orb=15.6654 +/- 0.0008 d. Finally, we discuss the observed flaring activity in the framework of quasi-spherical settling accretion, which is expected at the observed luminosities.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27931.title: The environments of type Ibn supernovae: evidence for a strong Wolf-Rayet star component
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27931.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27931v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Characterisation of progenitor stars of supernovae (SNe) poses several challenges. Direct observations of progenitors are based on serendipitious archival observations and are only possible for nearby events. Indirect methods include inferring nickel mass from the light curves or oxygen masses from the SN's nebular phase, both of which are tools to constrain the progenitor's initial mass. Alternatively, environments of SNe have been used as a proxy for the progenitor's age and metallicity. The progenitor channel of type Ibn SNe is a hotly debated topic. The mass-loss and the formation of He-rich circumstellar medium requires strong envelope stripping of the progenitor star. For core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe), this requires strong stellar wind mass losses, i.e. a Wolf-Rayet (WR) star, or binary interaction with a companion star. Here, we analyse a sample of host galaxies of type Ibn SNe that have been observed with MUSE. We use H$\alpha$ emission to infer the transient's association to star formation and derive the local metallicity with commonly used strong line diagnostic. We find that the sample of SNe are highly associated with star formation in the host galaxy, typically situated within one of the brightest HII regions in the host galaxy. The NCR distribution of H$\alpha$ pixels in SN Ibn environments strongly resembles that of WR stars, and shows a stronger preference to SF compared to other core-collapse SN types. Metallicity measurements show typically sub-solar metallicity in the SN environments.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27933.title: Probing Minihalos in the Late Dark Ages through Velocity Acoustic Oscillations in the 21-cm Power Spectrum
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27933.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the Dark Ages, minihalos above the Jeans mass accrete gas from the intergalactic medium (IGM). The accreted gas would be heated to virial temperature and produces 21 cm signal in emission, while the majority of gas retained in the IGM is cold and has 21 cm signal in absorption. The 21 cm signal of the IGM generally dominates over that of minihalos, making it difficult to extract the contribution of minihalos from the detected 21 cm signal. However, in the late Dark Ages, in regions where the gas has not yet been influenced by the radiation from Pop III stars, the 21 cm signal from the IGM is weak because collisional coupling has become less efficient. More importantly, the relic supersonic dark matter-baryon relative streaming velocities suppress the gas accretion of smaller minihalos and encode their large-scale coherent features into the 21 cm signal, generating the velocity acoustic oscillation (VAO) features on the 21 cm power spectrum. This offers a promising avenue for detecting minihalos. We found that, at $z\sim 15$ ($\sim 20$), the first peak of the net VAO wiggle at $k=0.05$ Mpc$^{-1}$ is $\sim 1.4\times 10^{-3}$ ($\sim 3.1\times 10^{-4}$) mK$^2$. With a total of 24 lunar nights/8064 hr (60 lunar nights/20160 hr) of integration, the signal from $z\sim 15$ ($\sim 20$) is detectable for an array composed of 82944 (278784) dipoles, spread over $\sim 3.5$ ($\sim 6.3$) km. If the small-scale matter power spectrum is enhanced and minihalos are much more numerous than in the standard $\Lambda$CDM model, the signal is detectable for an even smaller scale array.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27949.title: Constraining Solid HNCO and Its Environment in Open JWST Data with Laboratory Spectra
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27949.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The presence of HNCO in the gaseous phase is well known for the interstellar medium, but the molecule is not detected yet in the solid phase. We report the first laboratory-confirmed identification of solid HNCO at 2260 cm$^{-1}$ in open JWST data using laboratory infrared spectra. For that, we grew binary mixtures of HNCO with main constituents of interstellar ice using ISEAge setup at 10 K: HNCO:H$_2$O = 1:10, HNCO:CO = 1:10, HNCO:CO$_2$ = 1:10, HNCO:CH$_3$OH~=~1:10. We present transmission infrared spectra of pure HNCO and HNCO-bearing ices along with the corresponding band strengths at 10 K. The fitting of open JWST observational data with the laboratory reference spectra in a 10--23 K temperature range show that solid HNCO is predominantly located in the apolar layer rich in CO. The abundance of solid HNCO is approximately estimated as 0.04--0.15\% relative to solid H$_2$O. The positive correlation between HNCO and N$_2$O suggests their co-formation via the chemical route that includes solid N$_2$. The results are also supported by the numerical modeling of HNCO formation in protostellar objects with predicted abundance of 0.06--0.11\%. We calculated the upper limits for CH$_3$CN toward two protostars and evaluated its abundance to solid water using the spectroscopic fitting and modeling.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27969.title: VVV CL001: A strong candidate for the most ancient star cluster in the Galaxy
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27969.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Finding the oldest globular cluster of the Galaxy is important to constrain a lower limit on the age of the Galaxy and the Universe. VVV CL001 ([l,b]= [5.26,0.77]) is perhaps the most metal-poor ([Fe/H]~-2.2 dex) globular cluster in the Galactic bulge and a promising candidate to be the oldest globular cluster in the entire Milky Way. Due to its recent discovery and high extinction, its physical parameters, especially the distance and age, remain highly uncertain, yet they are essential to define it as an ancient native stellar system of the Milky Way. We aim to refine the distance and age of VVV CL001 using deep and high-quality photometry, to study its role in the formation of the Milky Way, and to determine whether it is the oldest Galactic globular cluster. We used J and KS observations to construct the deepest CMD of VVV CL001 to date, based on FourStar/Baade PSF photometry combined with HST near-IR wide-filter PSF photometry. We selected cluster members through proper motion calculations and the HDBSCAN algorithm, and assigned membership probabilities via Markov-Chain Monte Carlo iterations in a 5-dimensional parameter space. Using r band data from DECam/Blanco, we optically identified horizontal branch members and applied an isochrone-fitting technique to determine the cluster distance, while members around the main-sequence turn-off yielded the age from different isochrone sets. Finally, we refined the cluster orbital parameters. We obtained a distance of d = 7.34 +- 0.46 kpc, the most precise to date. We derived an age of 13.4 +- 0.4 Gyr, indicating that VVV CL001 is one of the oldest globular clusters in the Galaxy. The orbit confirms that the cluster belongs to the Galactic bulge, which, together with its age and metallicity, could link it to the early proto-Milky Way assembly, extending the metal-poor end of the known in situ globular clusters.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.27985.title: Understanding the formation of alpha-Fe bimodality in the Milky Way using constrained cosmological simulations of the Local Group
arxiv.org/abs/2610.27985.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.27985v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We use a novel suite of constrained cosmological simulations of the Local Group to investigate the formation of alpha--Fe bimodalities in stellar discs of Milky Way analogues. In agreement with past studies using the Auriga model, we show that in our simulations the high-alpha sequence forms in a merger-induced starburst, which further quenches star formation, allowing the new stellar populations to form at low [alpha/Fe]. Producing a bimodality that is prominent at large radii, with a significant [alpha/Fe] gap and overlapping metallicity as in the Milky Way, requires the quenching of star formation across all radii where the bimodality is observed. The quenching can be achieved either with a galaxy-wide starburst, or with a retrograde merger reducing angular momentum in the outer disc and allowing more efficient dilution by the metal-poor gas in the circumgalactic medium (CGM). We show that mergers can also tilt the disc, changing the direction of galactic outflows and enriching a larger volume of the CGM with galactic metals, leading to low [alpha/Fe] scatter in the subsequently formed low-alpha sequence. We argue that the slopes in [alpha/Fe] of the two alpha sequences are crucial in narrowing down the mechanism that leads to their formation. We additionally uncover an indirect role that mergers play in enhancing the accretion of metal-poor gas onto galaxies. The smoothly accreted gas can dominate the gas content in the CGM and aid in the formation of distinct chemical sequences, especially at the low-metallicity end.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28005.title: Phakoseismology: Asteroseismology of gravitationally microlensed stars
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28005.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Asteroseismology relies on disk-integrated photometry or radial velocities, in which geometric cancellation suppresses modes of high spherical degree ($l\geq4$). Observations are thus limited to deeply penetrating, low-degree modes, leaving the outer envelope inaccessible. We investigate whether a high-magnification microlensing event can temporarily lift this limitation by differentially magnifying the surface of an oscillating source star. We modelled the visibility of solar-like oscillations during microlensing, weighting the surface by limb darkening and the local magnification. We computed multiplet visibilities and the power distribution among azimuthal components, and built a likelihood model for recovering the 3D spin-axis orientation from resolved rotational multiplets. When the lens-source separation becomes comparable to the source's angular radius, the magnification gradient acts as a transient spatial filter that breaks the symmetry of disk integration, raising high-degree mode visibilities by up to three orders of magnitude. The same non-axisymmetric weighting makes the relative power of azimuthal components depend on both the inclination and sky-projected azimuth of the spin axis, imprinting the full spin orientation onto the power spectrum. With $5\%$ relative-power uncertainties, we recover the orientation to $\sigma_i=2.9^\circ$ and $\sigma_\gamma=11.5^\circ$. Microlensing thus does more than amplify distant stars: its magnification pattern enables spatially selective asteroseismology. The effect is strongest for rare close encounters and unlikely to support large samples, and the newly visible high-degree modes will overlap with rotationally split and mixed modes, complicating mode identification. Nevertheless, individual high-quality events may open a window on envelope physics and spin geometries for stars in the Galactic bulge and beyond.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28006.title: An improvement to the spatial discretisation in the Astrophysical Weighted Particle Hydrodynamics method
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28006.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The discretisation of space in the Astrophysical Weighted Particle Hydrodynamics method is attained through a partition-of-unity-based cubature rule. The node (particle) weights in such rules must in general be obtained using approximations, for which only one has been thus far proposed in the literature. In this work, new approximations for these weights are proposed, their properties are studied, and their impact on the accuracy of the cubature rule and the overall method is assessed. Approximations for node centroids are also proposed and studied, and their possible applications are laid out. Additionally, for schemes in which the kernel-function compact-support size is set to be constant, rather than adaptive, weight and centroid approximations are provided as well. Finally, for the cubature rule arising from the weight approximation previously proposed in the literature, an asymptotic expression for its mean relative error is derived, and its usefulness for understanding the finite-sample properties of the cubature rule is showcased with some simple examples.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28013.title: Kinematically isolating intracluster light in AS1063: a distinct stellar population tracing the dark matter core
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28013.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a technique using integral-field spectroscopy to kinematically isolate intracluster light (ICL) from the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), enabling insights into their contrasting stellar populations and the inner dark matter halo profile. Applying this technique to MUSE data of Abell S1063, we find that both components are old (~9 Gyr), but the ICL is more metal-poor than the BCG, implying distinct progenitor pathways. Within 100 kpc, the ICL comprises 55 per cent of the BCG+ICL stellar mass - substantially more than inferred from photometric decompositions. The BCG and ICL possess distinct velocity distributions, which remain nearly constant with radius, with an ICL velocity dispersion more than twice that of the BCG, and a line-of-sight velocity offset of 86 +- 18 km/s. Two-dimensional S\'ersic fits yield an ICL centroid offset of 5.2 +- 1.5 kpc from the BCG. These phase-space offsets are indicative of the BCG oscillating in a broad potential minimum. Furthermore, the ICL surface-brightness profile matches that of strong-lensing estimates assuming a cored halo. Simulations indicate that the inner halo profile varies systematically for different dark matter models. Applied to larger samples, our method therefore offers a complementary route to testing the nature of dark matter, while simultaneously revealing the stellar origins of the ICL.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28034.title: Rapid Variability of Radiative Signatures from Driven Relativistic Reconnection
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28034.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28034v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rapid variability in energetic flares is a distinctive feature of high-energy emission from many magnetically dominated astrophysical sources. We investigate the radiative variability of driven relativistic magnetic reconnection using Particle-in-Cell simulations of strongly magnetized flux tubes pushed to merge at driving speed $v_{\rm push}$. This setup captures the onset of reconnection and provides a controlled model for single reconnection-driven flares near compact objects, where magnetic structures can be twisted, sheared, and forced to merge by turbulent accretion flows or relativistic frame dragging. We find that the merger efficiently accelerates particles into nonthermal distributions, producing synchrotron emission whose variability tracks the reconnection phases. We identify two regimes: a quasi-steady, weakly driven regime for $v_{push}\leq0.1\,c$, and strongly driven regime for $v_{\rm push}>0.1\,c$. The transition occurs when the driving exceeds the typical inflow-to-outflow velocity ratio of $\sim0.1$ in steady collisionless relativistic reconnection, i.e., the average rate at which reconnection can process incoming flux, potentially providing an additional source of variability. The lightcurves rise on $1$--$3$ light-crossing times of the reconnecting region, and the particle spectra develop power laws with index $p\simeq1.8$--$2.4$. These timescales are compatible with observed variability in high-energy sources, including the very-high-energy flares of M87$^*$ and the $\gamma$-ray flares of the Crab Nebula, making this model a viable framework for rapid flaring in active galactic nuclei and pulsar wind nebulae.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28049.title: On the superbursts as photodisintegrators of ashes from the rp-process -- Numerical simulations of superbursts with MESA II
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28049.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28049v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context: Superbursts are energetic explosions in the crusts of neutron stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs). At temperatures above 4 GK, photodisintegration of heavy rp-process ashes may play a major role alongside $^{12}$C fusion. Aims: We investigate how photodisintegration of rp-process ashes affects superburst properties and the initial $^{12}$C abundance required for ignition. Methods: We simulate superbursts with MESA v.24.08.1. Besides the canonical fuel of $20\%$ $^{12}$C and $80\%$ $^{56}$Fe, we test different $^{12}$C abundances mixed with scaled rp-process ashes. Results: Superbursts can ignite with only $10\%$ $^{12}$C when the remaining $90\%$ consists of rp-process ashes. Their luminosity is comparable to that of the canonical fuel, whereas $10\%$ $^{12}$C mixed with $90\%$ $^{56}$Fe yields lower luminosity. $^{56}$Fe remains the most abundant ash nuclide. Although photodisintegration drives nucleosynthesis, neutron, proton and alpha captures release energy at late times. We also find that $A=64$ nuclides or $^{20}$Ne help reduce the $^{12}$C abundance needed for ignition. Conclusions: The composition of accreted material - not just its $^{12}$C content - substantially affects superburst ignition, luminosity and nucleosynthesis.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28068.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28068.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langle\sigma v\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28073.title: Pulsar J1909+0749 and Supernova Remnant G42.1-0.2: A case of a pulsar that has exited the shell of its associated supernova remnant
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28073.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28073v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: (Abridged) The ATNF pulsar catalogue features only 63 pulsars that are possibly associated with a supernova remnant (SNR). Even rarer is the scenario in which the pulsar has escaped the physical extent of its corresponding SNR. We aim to identify the serendipitously discovered shell-type object G42.1-0.2 as a SNR. The known pulsar (PSR) J1909+0749 lies well outside the shell of SNR G42.1-0.2, but it has a cometary tail pointing towards the centre of the SNR; we propose that the SNR and the pulsar originated from the same supernova explosion. By measuring the flux densities of the shell G42.1-0.2 from ${\sim}$200 MHz to ${\sim}$6 GHz, we establish the nonthermal nature of its emission. With the characteristic age of the pulsar, its distance from the Sun estimated from the dispersion measure (DM), and the angular separation between the pulsar and the centre of the shell, we infer the evolutionary state of the SNR and the transverse velocity of the pulsar. Using proper motion measurements, we compare the SNR-pulsar direction with the velocity of the pulsar. The radio spectral index of the shell is $-0.36 \pm 0.08$, confirming that the emission is primarily nonthermal synchrotron. The proper motion measurements are not well constrained, but the amplitude and the direction are consistent with the interpretation that the SNR and the pulsar are associated. If the characteristic age and the DM-based distance represent the true age and the true distance of the pulsar and the SNR, then the standard evolution equations suggest that the SNR must still be in the Sedov-Taylor phase, evolving in a medium with a density of about 1.5 cm$^{-3}$. In addition, as a result of the PSR-SNR association, the transverse velocity of the pulsar PSR J1909+0749 is estimated to be ${\sim}1460~\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$, ranking it among the highest transverse velocities observed for pulsars in the Milky Way.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28117.title: The T-matrix method for modeling the optical properties of grains in exoplanetary atmospheres
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28117.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28117v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Observations of exoplanetary atmospheres have revealed a rather complex co-existence between the gaseous and condensed phases, ranging from atmospheres apparently covered in clouds to clear ones, across a myriad of intermediate regimes. The interaction between solids and stellar radiation is of fundamental importance when forward or retrieval models are compared to observations. The simplest approach is to assume spherical particles, whose scattering and absorption properties are readily computed with Mie theory. More advanced computational methods, however, can also treat non-spherical condensates. Among these, the transition matrix approach has proven to provide a rigorous and efficient calculation of the extinction by non-spherical particles over a broad range of sizes and refractive indices. We here focus on the absorption and scattering cross sections of forsterite, spinel and silicon monoxide from the near to the far infrared range for particles of different sizes, with shapes ranging from compact ensembles of spheres to porous aggregates. We find that, depending on the size and the configuration chosen, the differences in extinction can be as high as a factor of 2-3, with structured grains being more efficient absorbers in the near infrared for sizes greater than 1 $\mu$m. In a fiducial transmission spectrum we show that in the $\lambda = 1-5\,\mu$m range the amount of spherical material needed to match the contribution of the structured grains can be a factor 2 higher. Such calculations, available for the community through a Zenodo repository, prove to be useful for interpreting recent and future observations of exoplanetary atmospheres.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28123.title: Deriving Interplanetary Sector Boundary Crossings using Potential Field Source Surface Modeling
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28123.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) and associated interplanetary sector boundaries fundamentally structure the solar wind environment, modulating coronal mass ejection (CME) evolution and solar energetic particle transport. In this study, we evaluate the capability of a static Potential Field Source Surface (PFSS; $R_{ss}=2.5R_\odot$) coronal model to directly map interplanetary sector boundary crossings from the Sun to 1 au without dynamic heliospheric propagation models. We compare ballistically transported HCS crossings derived from GONG-ADAPT and SDO/HMI magnetic maps against sector boundary crossing observations from the SBCross catalog. PFSS modeling reproduces the large-scale interplanetary magnetic field topology well ($J\approx0.50$), achieving hit rates (POD) of 0.64 for GONG-ADAPT and 0.76 for HMI. Carrington synoptic maps outperform flux-transport modeled maps, suggesting that the short-term observational noise from data assimilation degrades topological matching more than map "aging". Predictive skill shows a strong solar cycle dependence, performing significantly better during solar maxima (POD=0.70-0.81) than solar minima (POD=0.56-0.67), attributed to more distinct crossings due to higher HCS inclination angles during maximum. Matched events exhibit travel times close to ballistic estimates of 4.8-4.9 days with an average timing difference centered near zero ($\pm1.1$ days) and 90% of events within $\pm 1.8$ days. The hit rate of HCS structures that interact with CMEs does not degrade (POD = 0.67-0.83), despite propagating $\approx7$ hours faster on average, implying that the CME interaction causes only minor structural changes to the HCS. Larger timing differences (>24 hours) are associated with flatter current sheets. Overall, static PFSS extrapolations offer a computationally inexpensive, effective approach for mapping global sector boundary structure.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28139.title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28139.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28139v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 255~eV suprathermal electron pitch angle distributions (PAD) data, our algorithm reliably captures large-scale polarity transitions, with $76\%$ of detected SBCs exhibiting clear HPS signatures ($\beta > 1$, $n_{\mathrm{peak}} > 10\mathrm{\,cm^{-3}}$).
